readings.title: The Ark Leads the Way
readings.subtitle: The Waters Stand in a Heap
readings.text: [Joshua 3:1] And Yehoshua rose early in the morning, and they set out from Shittim and came to the Yarden, he and all the children of Yisra’el, and lodged there before they passed over. [2] And it came to be after three days that the officers went through the midst of the camp, [3] and they commanded the people, saying, “When you see the ark of the covenant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, and the priests, the Lewites, bearing it, then you shall set out from your place and go after it. [4] “Only, keep a distance between you and it, about two thousand cubits by measure. Do not come near it, so that you know which way to go, for you have not passed over this way heretofore.” [5] And Yehoshua said to the people, “Set yourselves apart, for tomorrow <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> does wonders in your midst.” [6] And Yehoshua spoke to the priests, saying, “Take up the ark of the covenant and pass over before the people.” So they took up the ark of the covenant and went before the people. [7] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Yehoshua, <dq>“This day <dn>I</dn> begin to make you great in the eyes of all Yisra’el, so that they know that <dn>I</dn> am with you as <dn>I</dn> was with Mosheh.</dq> [8] <dq>“And you, command the priests who bear the ark of the covenant, saying, ‘When you come to the edge of the water of the Yarden, stand in the Yarden.’ ”</dq> [9] And Yehoshua said to the children of Yisra’el, “Come here, and hear the words of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>.” [10] And Yehoshua said, “By this you shall know that the living <dn>El</dn> is in your midst, and that <dn>He</dn> shall certainly drive out from before you the Kenaʽanite and the Ḥittite and the Ḥiwwite and the Perizzite and the Girgashite and the Amorite and the Yeḇusite: [11] “See, the ark of the covenant of the <dn>Master</dn> of all the earth is passing over before you into the Yarden. [12] “And now, take for yourselves twelve men from the tribes of Yisra’el, one man from every tribe. [13] “And it shall be, as soon as the soles of the feet of the priests who bear the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, the <dn>Master</dn> of all the earth, come to rest in the waters of the Yarden, that the waters of the Yarden are cut off, the waters that come down from upstream, and stand as a heap.” [14] And it came to be, when the people set out from their tents to pass over the Yarden, with the priests bearing the ark of the covenant before the people, [15] and as those bearing the ark came to the Yarden, and the feet of the priests bearing the ark dipped in the edge of the water – now the Yarden overflows all its banks during all the time of harvest – [16] that the waters which came down from upstream stood still, and rose in a heap very far away at Aḏam, the city that is beside Tsarethau. And the waters going down into the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, were completely cut off. And the people passed over opposite Yeriḥo. [17] And the priests bearing the ark of the covenant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> stood firm on dry ground in the midst of the Yarden. And all Yisra’el passed over on dry ground, until all the nation had completely passed over the Yarden.

readings.title: Stones of Remembrance
readings.subtitle: A Sign for Future Generations
readings.text: [Joshua 4:1] And it came to be, when all the nation had completely passed over the Yarden, that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Yehoshua, saying, [2] <dq>“Take for yourselves twelve men from the people, one man from every tribe,</dq> [3] <dq>“and command them, saying, ‘Take for yourselves twelve stones from here, out of the midst of the Yarden, from the place where the priests’ feet stood firm. And you shall bring them over with you and leave them in the lodging place where you lodge tonight.’ ”</dq> [4] And Yehoshua called the twelve men whom he had appointed from the children of Yisra’el, one man from every tribe, [5] and Yehoshua said to them, “Pass over before the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> into the midst of the Yarden, and each one of you take up a stone on his shoulder, according to the number of the tribes of the children of Yisra’el, [6] so that this becomes a sign among you when your children ask in time to come, saying, ‘What are these stones to you?’ [7] “Then you shall say to them that the waters of the Yarden were cut off before the ark of the covenant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. When it passed over the Yarden, the waters of the Yarden were cut off. And these stones shall be for a remembrance to the children of Yisra’el forever.” [8] And the children of Yisra’el did so, as Yehoshua commanded, and took up twelve stones from the midst of the Yarden, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had spoken to Yehoshua, according to the number of the tribes of the children of Yisra’el, and brought them over with them to the lodging place, and left them there. [9] And Yehoshua set up twelve stones in the midst of the Yarden, in the place where the feet of the priests who bore the ark of the covenant stood. And they are there to this day. [10] And the priests who bore the ark stood in the midst of the Yarden until every matter was finished that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had commanded Yehoshua to speak to the people, according to all that Mosheh had commanded Yehoshua. And the people hastened and passed over. [11] And it came to be, when all the people had completely passed over, that the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and the priests passed over in the presence of the people. [12] And the sons of Re’uḇen, and the sons of Gad, and half the tribe of Menashsheh passed over armed before the children of Yisra’el, as Mosheh had spoken to them. [13] About forty thousand armed ones for battle passed over before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> for battle, to the plains of Yeriḥo. [14] On that day <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> made Yehoshua great in the eyes of all Yisra’el. And they feared him as they had feared Mosheh, all the days of his life. [15] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Yehoshua, saying, [16] <dq>“Command the priests who bear the ark of the Witness, to come up from the Yarden.”</dq> [17] And Yehoshua commanded the priests, saying, “Come up from the Yarden.” [18] And it came to be, when the priests who bore the ark of the covenant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had come from the midst of the Yarden, and the soles of the priests’ feet touched the dry land, that the waters of the Yarden returned to their place and flowed over all its banks as before. [19] And the people came up from the Yarden on the tenth day of the first month, and they camped in Gilgal on the east border of Yeriḥo. [20] And those twelve stones which they took out of the Yarden, Yehoshua set up in Gilgal. [21] And he spoke to the children of Yisra’el, saying, “When your children ask their fathers in time to come, saying, ‘What are these stones?’ [22] then you shall let your children know, saying, ‘Yisra’el passed over this Yarden on dry land.’ [23] “For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> dried up the waters of the Yarden before you until you had passed over, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> did to the Sea of Reeds, which <dn>He</dn> dried up before us until we had passed over, [24] so that all the peoples of the earth might know the hand of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, that it is mighty, so that you shall fear <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> forever.” [Joshua 5:1] And it came to be, when all the sovereigns of the Amorites who were beyond the Yarden westward, and all the sovereigns of the Kenaʽanites who were by the sea, heard that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had dried up the waters of the Yarden from before the children of Yisra’el until we had passed over, that their heart melted, and there was no more spirit in them because of the presence of the children of Yisra’el.

readings.title: Rolling Away the Reproach
readings.subtitle: Circumcision and Passover at Gilgal
readings.text: [Joshua 5:2] At that time <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Yehoshua, <dq>“Make flint knives for yourself, and circumcise the sons of Yisra’el again the second time.”</dq> [3] So Yehoshua made flint knives for himself, and circumcised the sons of Yisra’el at the Hill of Foreskins. [4] And this is the reason why Yehoshua circumcised them: All the people who came out of Mitsrayim who were males, all the men of war, had died in the wilderness on the way, after they came out of Mitsrayim. [5] For all the people who came out had been circumcised, but all the people born in the wilderness, on the way as they came out of Mitsrayim, had not been circumcised. [6] For the children of Yisra’el walked forty years in the wilderness, till all the nation – the men of war who came out of Mitsrayim – were consumed, because they did not obey the voice of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, to whom <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> swore that <dn>He</dn> would not show them the land which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had sworn to their fathers that <dn>He</dn> would give us, a land flowing with milk and honey. [7] And <dn>He</dn> raised up their sons in their place. Them Yehoshua circumcised, for they were uncircumcised, because they had not been circumcised on the way. [8] And it came to be, when they had completed circumcising all the nation, that they stayed in their places in the camp till they were healed. [9] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Yehoshua, <dq>“Today I have rolled away the reproach of Mitsrayim from you.”</dq> So the name of the place is called Gilgal to this day. [10] And the children of Yisra’el camped in Gilgal, and performed the Pesaḥ on the fourteenth day of the month at evening in the plains of Yeriḥo. [11] And they ate of the stored grain of the land on the morrow after the Pesaḥ, unleavened bread and roasted grain on this same day. [12] And the manna ceased on the day after they had eaten the stored grain of the land. And the children of Yisra’el no longer had manna, but they ate the fruit of the land of Kenaʽan that year.

readings.title: The Conquest of Jericho
readings.subtitle: The Walls Fall Down
readings.text: [Joshua 5:13] And it came to be, when Yehoshua was by Yeriḥo, that he lifted his eyes and looked, and saw a Man standing opposite him with <dn>His</dn> sword drawn in <dn>His</dn> hand. And Yehoshua went to <dn>Him</dn> and said to <dn>Him</dn>, “Are <dn>You</dn> for us or for our adversaries?” [14] And <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>“No, for <dn>I</dn> have now come as <dn>Captain</dn> of the host of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.”</dq> And Yehoshua fell on his face to the earth and did obeisance, and said to <dn>Him</dn>, “What does my <dn>Master</dn> say to <dn>His</dn> servant?” [15] And the <dn>Captain</dn> of the host of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Yehoshua, <dq>“Take your sandal off your foot, for the place where you stand is set-apart.”</dq> And Yehoshua did so. [Joshua 6:1] And Yeriḥo was shut up tight because of the children of Yisra’el. None went out, and none came in. [2] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Yehoshua, <dq>“See! <dn>I</dn> have given Yeriḥo into your hand, its sovereign, and the mighty men of valour.</dq> [3] <dq>“And you shall go around the city, all the men of battle, going around the city once. Do this for six days.</dq> [4] <dq>“And seven priests bear seven rams’ horns before the ark. And on the seventh day you go around the city seven times, and the priests blow the horns.</dq> [5] <dq>“And it shall be, when they make a long blast with the ram’s horn, and when you hear the sound of the horn, that all the people shout with a great shout. And the wall of the city shall fall down flat, and the people shall go up every man straight before him.”</dq> [6] And Yehoshua son of Nun called the priests, and said to them, “Take up the ark of the covenant, and let seven priests bear seven rams’ horns before the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.” [7] And he said to the people, “Go, and go around the city, and let him who is armed go on before the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.” [8] And it came to be, when Yehoshua had spoken to the people, that the seven priests bearing the seven rams’ horns before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> passed over and blew the horns, and the ark of the covenant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> went after them. [9] And the armed men went before the priests who blew the horns, and the rear guard came after the ark, going and blowing the horns. [10] And Yehoshua had commanded the people, saying, “Do not shout or cause your voice to be heard, nor let any word come out of your mouth, until the day I say to you, ‘Shout!’ Then you shall shout.” [11] So he had the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> go around the city, going around once. And they came into the camp and stayed in the camp. [12] And Yehoshua rose early in the morning, and the priests took up the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [13] And seven priests bearing seven rams’ horns before the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> were walking, going and blowing the horns, and the armed men went before them. But the rear guard came after the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, going and blowing the horns. [14] And on the second day they went around the city once and returned to the camp. Thus they did six days. [15] And it came to be on the seventh day that they rose early, about the dawning of the day, and went around the city seven times in this manner. Only on that day they went around the city seven times. [16] And it came to be at the seventh time, when the priests blew the horns, that Yehoshua said to the people, “Shout, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has given you the city! [17] “And the city shall be put under the ban, it and all that is in it belongs to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. Only Raḥaḇ the whore shall live, she and all who are with her in the house, because she hid the messengers that we sent. [18] “And you, by all means guard yourselves from that which is under the ban, lest you come under the ban when you take of that which is under the ban, and make the camp of Yisra’el a curse, and trouble it. [19] “But all the silver and gold, and vessels of bronze and iron, are set-apart to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, they go into the treasury of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.” [20] And the people shouted when the priests blew the horns. And it came to be when the people heard the sound of the horn, and the people shouted with a great shout, that the wall fell down flat. And the people went up into the city, every man straight before him, and they captured the city. [21] And they put under the ban all that was in the city, both man and woman, young and old, and ox and sheep and donkey, with the edge of the sword. [22] And Yehoshua said to the two men who had spied out the land, “Go into the house of the woman, the whore, and bring out the woman and all that she has, as you swore to her.” [23] And the young men, the spies, went in and brought out Raḥaḇ, and her father, and her mother, and her brothers, and all that she had. So they brought out all her relatives and set them outside the camp of Yisra’el. [24] And they burned the city and all that was in it with fire. Only the silver and gold, and the vessels of bronze and of iron, they put into the treasury of the house of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [25] And Yehoshua saved Raḥaḇ the whore alive, and her father’s household, and all that she had. And she dwelt in the midst of Yisra’el to this day, because she hid the messengers whom Yehoshua sent to spy out Yeriḥo. [26] And Yehoshua warned them at that time, saying, “Cursed is the man before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> who rises up and builds this city Yeriḥo – he lays its foundation with his first-born, and with his youngest he sets up its gates.” [27] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was with Yehoshua, and his report was in all the land.
